# Per-site unsupervised baselines and calibrated alerting for BACnet/IP on ProtoSense

## Verified facts
- ArmaturaSec states it holds no capture containing a confirmed attack — none of its clients has ever provided one — but has several terabytes of captures from consenting clients collected over the past three years. [F1]
- ProtoSense is the company's passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic, so a detector for it must address both protocols. [F2]
- Operational acceptance is the bar: an earlier supervised classifier flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off, and alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language. [F3]
- The company needs on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency, and intends a fifth hardware variant in late 2025 with a dedicated security processor. [F4]
- Company-side capacity is one to two engineers part-time, with traffic archives, hardware bench and existing firmware codebase available under NDA. [F5]
- Kiss's stated openness covers joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions and contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment. [F6]
- Her published work includes per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed and a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data. [F7]
- Her group also reports 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target and an incremental Gaussian mixture model for online detection without the need for periodic full retraining. [F8]

## Our inference
- Kiss's interest in a joint project is documented, but her availability is not stated anywhere in the material, so this proposal is conditional on her confirming capacity; that likely sets the start date more than the technical scope.
- Her supplied evidence covers Modbus/TCP, DNP3, PROFINET and OPC UA but not BACnet/IP; protocol-agnostic byte-level features suggest a route across, but they do not establish that BACnet detection will work.
- Whether a calibrated false-alarm rate stays low enough to avoid the alert fatigue ArmaturaSec already met on client sites is the main operational risk, especially once site-specific baselines drift with seasonal load and planned process changes.

## Proposed next steps
- First experiment (proposed, about four months): test whether Kiss's baseline-plus-calibration approach transfers to BACnet/IP. Sample: held-out normal BACnet/IP captures from at least two ArmaturaSec client sites plus her testbed, with anomalies injected one factor at a time — object/instance writes, timing offsets, payload substitution — so the result says which factor drives detection. Baselines: a fixed-threshold rule detector and her Modbus-trained detector applied unchanged. Measure false alarms per site per day, detection per anomaly type, and whether each alert renders as one plain-language sentence. Go/no-go: alarm volume a pilot client would keep enabled, at least one anomaly the rule baseline misses, and one explanation a plant manager accepts; otherwise stop and re-scope features. Kiss contributes method and testbed; ArmaturaSec contributes captures and engineer time.
- Proposed second step: apply the unlabelled-data threshold calibration to a multi-site, twelve-month archive to test drift, proposing a target of nominal and observed false-alarm rates within one percentage point and a quarterly recalibration schedule as negotiation targets.
- Proposed third step: run the chosen detector on the ProtoSense bench and measure per-window inference time against the forwarding cycle on both the current appliance and the planned security-processor variant, proposing a target of staying inside ten percent of the cycle.
- Proposed fourth step: co-design the alert explanation with two client plant managers and measure whether they can judge an alert actionable unaided, proposing a target of four out of five alerts judged correctly.

## Open questions
- Does Krisztina Kiss have availability and supervisory capacity for a joint project in the coming academic year, and can her group's testbed data-sharing agreement be applied to ArmaturaSec?
- Which ArmaturaSec archives and BACnet/IP captures can be shared under NDA, for which sites and periods, and do any of them carry known incidents or operator annotations?
- Should the first prototype target the existing ProtoSense/NetGuard appliances or the planned late-2025 security-processor variant, and what resource budget applies?
- What false-alarm rate, alert volume and explanation format would ArmaturaSec's clients and plant managers accept in a pilot?
- Should the first experiment prioritise Modbus TCP, where Kiss has direct published evidence, or BACnet/IP, where the company needs coverage but her material shows a gap?
